sop-from-memo.output:
WATER HEATER SWAP · You will need · Steps · Done looks like · Common mistakes.

YOU WILL NEED
- Main water shut-off valve (at meter)
- Electrical breaker for water heater
- Garden hose from van
- Floor drain access
- Two new flex lines (hot and cold)
- Expansion tank (ASK OWNER: when required)
- Camera for file photo

STEPS

1. Shut the main water valve at the meter — turn clockwise until it stops, do not rely on the isolation valve near the tank.

2. Switch off the breaker for the water heater at the panel.

3. Run the garden hose from the van to the floor drain and open the tank drain valve fully until water stops flowing.

4. Disconnect the old flex lines from inlet and outlet.

5. Remove the old water heater from its space.

6. Place the new water heater in position.

7. Connect two new flex lines (one hot, one cold) — replace every time, do not reuse old lines.

8. Fill the tank by opening the main water valve.

9. Open the closest faucet (hot side) until water runs steady with no air sounds.

10. Switch the breaker back on.

11. Wait 20 minutes, then inspect all connections and the floor underneath for water drips or pooling.

12. Take a photo of the completed install for the file.

DONE LOOKS LIKE
- No water leaks at any connection after 20 minutes
- Tank is full and hot water runs clear at faucets
- Photo is in the job file
- Old unit and hose are removed from the site

COMMON MISTAKES
1. Skipping the main valve and trusting the small isolation valve — you end up with pressure in the lines during disconnect. Check by closing the main, waiting 30 seconds, then opening the drain valve; if water still flows, the main valve did not seal.

2. Powering the heater before air is bled — you can trap air in the line and the tank won't heat properly. Check by running hot water at the nearest faucet for a full minute; air will sputter, water should run smooth.

3. Forgetting the expansion tank when there is a check valve on the main line — pressure builds with nowhere to go and can crack the new tank. ASK OWNER: does this job site have a check valve on the main, and is an expansion tank already in place or needed?
